subject: Performance SLO qualification: p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider) - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — performance targets and next steps

Alex — great talking earlier. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of your requirements (please correct anything I get wrong):
- End-to-end p95 target: <= 250ms (per your product team goal)
- End-to-end p99 target: <= 500ms (hard SLO)
- Concurrent API concurrency target: 150 concurrent requests during peak cadence
- Sustained throughput: ~3k tokens/sec across 10 worker processes (typical usage pattern)
- Streaming support required: yes (partial stream + final output)
- Typical input size: median prompt ~120 tokens, 95th ~800 tokens (includes user messages + context)

What we will do next: 
1) Aditya will review your synthetic capture and advise on expected p95/p99 on Redwood hosted API vs your current provider.
2) You’ll share the traffic_profile.json + perf capture (attachment) and a short sample of production traces (latency_summary.csv).
3) If numbers look good, we’ll schedule a short PoC (1-week) with representative traffic to validate end-to-end latency and streaming behavior.
4) We’ll align on acceptance criteria (p95/p99, error budget, and concurrency testing windows) and sign off on a simple mutual action plan.

Can you confirm the targets above and attach the capture when it’s convenient? I’ll start lining up a small test cluster to run an apples-to-apples comparison.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

[Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and next steps

Thanks Marissa — that look right to me. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- p95 target: our product PM set 200ms as the aspirational goal, but we can accept up to 250ms for go-live. p99 must stay <= 500ms.
- Concurrency: 150 concurrent inference calls is correct for peak spikes; baseline concurrency is closer to 40-60.
- Streaming: important for us — we stream partial generations to UI (low-latency first tokens matter).

I’ve attached the perf capture + latency_summary.csv and a quick traffic_profile.json that contains the distribution you asked for. The perf capture is a set of client-side traces captured over a 1-hour test. 

Also: current provider (ProviderX) p95 320ms, p99 ~780ms (end-to-end measured from our front-end). We want to validate that Redwood hosted can consistently hit p95 ~200–250ms in our baseline scenarios, and p99 under 500ms with our realistic traffic.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Director of Engineering | Finlytics Inc.
alex.chen@finlytics.ai

Attachments: finlytics_perf_capture.zip, latency_summary.csv, traffic_profile.json
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and next steps

Thanks Alex — appreciate the data. Quick technical notes / asks so we can scope the PoC correctly: 

1) Workload profile: the traffic_profile.json is perfect. Can you also confirm the percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming? Even a coarse split (e.g., 60/40) helps size our streaming slots.
2) Tokenization: are the token counts you provided after tokenization or raw characters? We need tokenized counts to estimate KV-cache size.
3) TLS termination and any additional front-end hops — we’ll run tests end-to-end but want to know if you have a CDN or edge proxy that adds latency.

Planned host-side test approach: 
- Small Redwood hosted cluster with identical model weights used by your provider (we’ll use model parity where possible)
- Run replay of your capture at multiple scales: baseline (1x), spike (3x), sustained (0.8x over 10min windows)
- Measure p95/p99 end-to-end and token-level breakdown (network, model, kernel, serialization).

If you can confirm the streaming split and tokenization detail today, we can provision infra and run a first pass tomorrow.

-Aditya
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — performance targets and next steps

Hi Aditya — quick answers from our infra team: 
- Streaming split: ~65% streaming, ~35% non-streaming (mostly chat completions where we need partial tokens asap).
- Token counts: provided numbers are after tokenization (we used tiktoken v0.4.0 for the capture). Median 120 tokens, 95th percentile ~800 tokens.
- Front-end hops: we use CloudFront in front of an edge proxy (Fastly) which adds ~12–18ms on average depending on region; tests in the capture were collected from our US-west users so you should see that delta.

Attached: traffic_profile.json (small sanitized extract) and latency_summary.csv (aggregated traces). We don’t have permission to share full raw traces right now — can sign an NDA if needed.

Thanks —
Priya Shah
Infra Lead | Finlytics Inc.
priya.shah@finlytics.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap — performance targets and next steps

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn. Next steps from Redwood: 
- Aditya and team will provision a small hosted test cluster and run the replay with your attached traffic_profile + capture tomorrow (we’ll run baseline + spike runs).
- We’ll produce a short results deck that breaks down end-to-end p95/p99 and token-level latencies, and highlight any optimizations (batching, KV-cache tuning, streaming slot sizing).
- Tentative acceptance criteria for PoC: p95 <= 250ms for median/steady runs, p99 <= 500ms for steady runs, streaming first-token latency <= 120ms for 90% of streaming requests.
- I’ll schedule a 30-min results review next week and include a proposed mutual action plan with milestones for go-live.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll also send a simple NDA template so you can share any additional traces we’ll need for diagnosis.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the PoC.

Marissa Cole
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
